principles.text: Let a physical relationship that truly belongs to the shop (how its things rest, balance or meet, with the empty space around them as part of it) shape the skeleton of the page in static HTML and CSS, instead of a giant hero picture followed by content strips.

Connect the sections through one visual idea taken from the shop's own work rather than from decoration, and change scale and information density from one section to the next instead of repeating one module in every section.

When the shop states a sequence or several reasons, give each its own visual beat and rhythm. Do not show the same guide or scale twice, and do not let the distinctive first screen shrink into a conventional catalogue further down.

avoid.text: Keeping a generic skeleton (a top navigation bar, copy on one side, a giant hero picture, a strip of pictures) and only changing what is inside it.
Discarding the strongest element of the first screen while polishing the later sections.
Treating a good picture as if it proved a distinctive page skeleton.
